choices.text: Populations of symbiotic mycorrhiza that live in the soil would initially decline.
Unwanted plant species like thistles would be unable to survive.
The chance of survival of a beneficial native plant would increase.
The number of all types of beneficial microorganisms would increase in the long term.
Populations of other types of disease organisms would increase proportionally.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is most analogous to the process, described in the last paragraph, by which the spread of thistles can be curtailed?

explanationBlocks.heading: Anticipate
explanationBlocks.body: The microorganisms protect native plants against disease organisms. Healthier native plants can then compete with thistles. The intervention therefore checks one competitor indirectly by defending its rivals against a separate source of harm. Look for that three-way relationship rather than a direct attack on the unwanted competitor.

choices.text: A newspaper works to prevent Party A from winning a majority of seats in the legislature by publishing editorials encouraging that party's supporters to switch their allegiance and vote for candidates from a rival party.
choices.explanation:
"Preventing Party A from winning a majority of seats" could match up with "preventing thistles from overrunning the soil".

"The newspaper working to prevent that" could be the farmer / the beneficial microorganisms?

What would be the "party supporters to switch their allegiance to a rival party"? Is there something that was previously helping thistles that will now be helping the native plants to grow?

choices.text: A newspaper works to prevent Party A from winning a majority of seats in the legislature by publishing editorials defending candidates from a rival party against attacks by certain broadcast journalists.
choices.explanation: Party A corresponds to thistles; the rival party corresponds to native plants. The journalists attacks correspond to disease organisms, and the editorials defend the rivals just as beneficial microorganisms protect native plants. In each case, the intervention limits one competitors dominance indirectly by shielding its rivals from a separate attacker.

choices.text: A newspaper works to prevent Party A from winning a majority of seats in the legislature by publishing editorials intended to discourage supporters of Party A from voting in the upcoming election.
choices.explanation:
"Preventing Party A from winning a majority of seats" could match up with "preventing thistles from overrunning the soil".

"The newspaper working to prevent that" could be the farmer.
"the editorials" can be the old-school dirt with the microorganisms.

But, there's no great match for the idea that the microorganisms are "intended to discourage supporters" of thistle from showing up to vote.

The beneficial microorganisms are intended to fight the aggressive disease organisms, but it's weird to call the aggressive disease organisms "supporters of thistle". It sounds like the beneficial microorganisms protect the plant roots of the native plants from being attacked by the aggressive disease organisms.

So "discouraging attackers of native plants" is more the function of the "editorials" than is "discouraging supporters of thistle".

choices.text: A newspaper works to prevent Party A from winning a majority of seats in the legislature by publishing editorials attacking certain public figures who support candidates from Party A.
choices.tag: Weaker Match: support for Party A
choices.explanation:
Just like (C), we get into worse-match territory with the idea of something *supporting* thistle, when what we're really trying to combat (the aggressive disease organisms) is something that *attacks* the native plants.

Otherwise, this answer seems better than (C), because "going after public figures who support thistles" sounds a little more like the third-party that would match up with the aggressive disease organisms, whereas (C) was using "supporters of A" which sounds more directly related to thistle itself.

choices.text: A newspaper works to prevent Party A from winning a majority of seats in the legislature by publishing editorials intended to create antagonism between two factions within that party.
choices.explanation:
This answer is saying that the restoration researcher is trying to prevent thistle from dominating the soil by adding microorganisms intended to create an internal battle within the thistles.

But the microorganisms aren't related to the thistle directly. They're just protecting the native plants from having its roots attacked by aggressive disease organisms.
